title: Secretome proteomics of THP-1 macrophages under M0, M1, and M2 polarization
projectDescription: This dataset comprises label-free quantitative proteomics of the secretome from human THP-1 serglycin (SRGN) knock-out and wild-type macrophage-like cells differentiated with PMA (M0) and polarized to M1 (LPS + IFN-γ) or M2 (IL-4 + IL-13). The study investigates how macrophage activation states in the absence of serglycin reshape the composition of secreted proteins relevant to inflammatory signaling, vesicle biology, and metabolism. Conditioned media were collected after polarization, processed by bottom-up proteomics, and analyzed by nanoLC–MS/MS on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos. The resulting protein abundance profiles provide a resource to compare resting (M0) versus pro-inflammatory (M1) and alternatively activated (M2) macrophage secretomes in a standardized cell system.
sampleProcessingProtocol: THP-1 wild-type and serglycin knock-out monocytes were differentiated with 150 ng/mL PMA for 24 h and rested 24 h (M0), followed by polarization to M1 (100 ng/mL LPS + 20 ng/mL IFN-γ, 24 h) or M2 (20 ng/mL IL-4 + 20 ng/mL IL-13, 24 h). Cells were washed thoroughly in PBS and incubated for 24 h in serum- and phenol-free RPMI 1640 supplemented with 2 mM L-glutamine and 1% penicillin–streptomycin to collect secretomes. Conditioned media were clarified by centrifugation and 0.2 µm filtration and concentrated ~50× using 3 kDa MWCO centrifugal filters. Proteins were reduced (DTT), alkylated (IAA), and digested sequentially with Lys-C and trypsin. Peptides were cleaned using C18 tips, dried, and reconstituted in 0.1% formic acid before LC-MS/MS analysis on an EASY-nLC 1200 coupled to an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos using a 60-min C18 gradient under data-dependent acquisition.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw LC-MS/MS files were processed with MaxQuant v2.4.9.0 using the human UniProt database, and proteins annotated as reverse hits, potential contaminants, or “only identified by site” were removed. LFQ intensities were log2-transformed, and proteins were retained if detected in at least two replicates in any condition. Missing values were imputed in R using the DEP package (“manual” method, shift = 1.8, scale = 0.3). Differential abundance analysis was performed with limma using voom-like mean-variance modeling and empirical Bayes moderation, and p-values were adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg method without applying an explicit fold-change cutoff.
